title: IC Substrate Inspection - Edge Placement Error Detection on 2920 Series
subtitle: Post-Clean Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Wei Zhang

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the 2920 Series system to detect and classify Edge Placement Error defects during post-clean inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Edge Placement Error defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the 2920 Series platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: 2920 Series
- Inspection Type: IC Substrate Inspection
- Target Defect: Edge Placement Error
- Process Step: Post-Clean
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all 2920 Series systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-clean monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: 2920 Series
Software Version: v9.1.281
Recipe: IC_SUBSTRATE_INSPECTION_14nm_POST_CLEAN
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (136 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the 2920 Series system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'IC Substrate Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Edge Placement Error defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 69 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 90% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.1% for IC Substrate Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-29
Wafers Tested: 26
Total Defects Found: 3611
Defect Density: 1149.42 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.8%
Capture Rate: 95.2%
Test Duration: 148 minutes
System Uptime: 97.5%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The 2920 Series demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Edge Placement Error at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
